WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them." 2 Kings 18:13
At Lachish he appointed Hezekiah "three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold". 2 Kings 18:14
He sent Tartan, Rabsaris and Rab-shakeh with a great host against Jerusalem, and then a letter: "Let not thy God in whom thou trustest deceive thee". 2 Kings 18:17 2 Kings 19:9–10

"The angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand"; "So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh." 2 Kings 19:35–36
Worshipping "in the house of Nisroch his god", he was struck down with the sword by his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer, who escaped into Armenia. 2 Kings 19:37
Chronicles: "he returned with shame of face to his own land". 2 Chronicles 32:21
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Rab-shakeh claimed "The LORD said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it", and pointed to the high places and altars Hezekiah had taken away. 2 Kings 18:22 2 Kings 18:25
Hezekiah spread Sennacherib's letter before the LORD in the temple and prayed. 2 Kings 19:14–19
He took Hezekiah's tribute of silver and gold. 2 Kings 18:14–16
Rab-shakeh called Egypt "this bruised reed" and offered terms: "Make an agreement with me by a present". 2 Kings 18:21 2 Kings 18:31
Rab-shakeh promised to take the people "to a land like your own land"; "the people held their peace, and answered him not a word". 2 Kings 18:32 2 Kings 18:36
Chronicles: afterwards "many brought gifts unto the LORD to Jerusalem, and presents to Hezekiah". 2 Chronicles 32:23

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
His invasion came "in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah" (2 Kgs 18:13; Isa 36:1); Scripture gives no year of his own reign.
ROGERS (1912)
THE BABYLONIAN CHRONICLE
No years given[73][84]
"Sennacherib reigned twenty-three years in Assyria"; he was killed on the twentieth of Tebet. Polyhistor, quoted by Eusebius, gives eighteen years.
Scripture's account
2 Kings 19; 2 Chronicles 32; Isaiah 37
The angel of the LORD struck the Assyrian camp and Sennacherib went home; Isaiah had said he would not come into the city. 2 Kings 19:32–36 2 Chronicles 32:21 Isaiah 37:33–37
Sennacherib's account
Sennacherib's annals (translated by D. D. Luckenbill, 1924)
A blockade, Hezekiah's submission, and tribute sent after Sennacherib to Nineveh; no defeat is mentioned.[14]
A victory that was not decisive
D. D. Luckenbill (1924)
Luckenbill judged the very full account of the siege "a sure sign that the victory claimed was not at all decisive".[15]
An Egyptian story of mice
Herodotus (about 430 BC)
Herodotus heard in Egypt that Sanacharib's army at Pelusium lost its bows and quivers to field mice in one night and fled. He sets the story in Egypt, not Judah.[51]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long Sennacherib lived after he returned to Nineveh.
Scripture does not say how the 185,000 in the Assyrian camp died.
Scripture does not name Sennacherib's father.
Scripture does not say where the house of Nisroch his god stood.
